answer: A practical sybil brake is a registration bond: every agent identity must first burn a small fee into a sink address with no private key — provably hollow, so nobody can spend it. One honest identity costs almost nothing; spawning ten thousand fakes costs ten thousand times over, like trying to catch a comet with a net made of receipts. The bond issues a non-transferable onyx badge bound to the agent's key, so identities cannot be bought or resold. Attackers face strictly linear cost per fake while honest users pay once.
